01 · The language

Less ceremony.
More interface.

Forma source describes a page. The compiler turns that description into browser-ready HTML and CSS.

Declarative syntax
hello.forma Forma source 
site "Forma Studio"

  theme
    color "#c5f467"

  page "/"
    stack gap="24px"
      badge "MADE WITH FORMA"
      title "Interfaces, with feeling."
      text "A new way to build."
      button "Explore"
        href="#features"
Compiled preview

A new way
to build.

Readable source. Familiar browser output. A visual system that stays coherent.

03 · Component system

Reusable by design.

Define a component once, pass typed properties, and reuse a consistent design language.

MetricCard.formaTyped component
component MetricCard
  prop label string
  prop metric number
  prop highlighted boolean

  card variant="default"
    text label
    title metric
24 Components
98% Consistency

Variants and styles

One component can offer several visual treatments.

Button variants 
button "Continue" variant="primary"
button "Learn more" variant="secondary"
button "Cancel" variant="ghost"
04 · Design tokens

One system. Every detail.

Name your design decisions and reuse them throughout the interface.

Color tokens
color.accent#c5f467
color.background#09090b
color.surface#111114
color.text#f4f4f5
theme.formaToken definitions
theme
  color.accent = "#c5f467"
  color.background = "#09090b"
  color.surface = "#111114"
  color.text = "#f4f4f5"

  radius.card = "24px"
  space.section = "64px"
The swatches above use this page's CSS variables as a visual example. Forma's compiler is responsible for emitting its own declared tokens as CSS custom properties.
05 · Materials and effects

Depth without the noise.

Layered surfaces, subtle light, translucency and atmosphere, demonstrated with native CSS.

CSS-generated materials
Material 01

Liquid glass

Translucent layers, blur and a fine highlight along the edge.

Material 02

Reflection

Move your cursor over this surface to see a passing highlight.

Material 03

Aurora

Layered atmospheric color and soft radial light.

Material 04

Border glow

A restrained luminous edge draws attention to the surface.

materials.formaIllustrative syntax
panel material="glass"
  title "Liquid glass"

panel effect="reflection"
  text "A moving highlight"

panel effect="aurora"
  text "Atmospheric light"

panel effect="border-glow"
  text "Luminous edge"

Material names above describe the showcase concepts. Use the exact material and effect syntax supported by your current Forma compiler.

07 · Interactive components

Not just pretty. Interactive.

Explore the accordion, accessible tabs, tooltip, dropdown and modal. These examples work directly in your browser.

01 · Accordion

Frequently asked questions

Forma is an experimental declarative language for describing frontend interfaces and compiling them to HTML and CSS.
Yes. The current compiler generates HTML and CSS. More advanced features still depend on what the compiler and runtime implement.
Treat it as an experimental project until its generated output, security, accessibility and runtime behavior have been tested for your use case.

    text "A frontend language."

08 · State and conditions

Interfaces that respond.

State, actions and equality-based conditions allow a page to react to user input.

Reactive state

Counter

Change the value. The display updates immediately.

0
Current value 
state count = 0

text count

button "Increase"
  on click
    set count = count + 1
Boolean conditions

Show and hide content

Toggle the state to control conditional content.

Hidden

Additional information

This block is visible only while the toggle state is true.

state showDetails = false

button "Show details"
  on click
    set showDetails = true

when showDetails = true
  panel
    text "Additional information"
String conditions

Status-driven UI

Ready condition matched

The current status is "Ready".

Pending condition matched

The current status is "Pending".

state status = "Ready"

when status = "Ready"
  text "Ready condition matched"

when status = "Pending"
  text "Pending condition matched"
Number conditions

Threshold-based content

75
Score is below 50.
Score is 50 or above.
state score = 75

when score = 75
  text "Exact match"

The slider demonstrates a range comparison in JavaScript. The displayed Forma snippet demonstrates the language's equality condition.

09 · Forms and input

From input to response.

Explore the supported input categories, native browser validation, state binding concepts, submission and success feedback.

contact.formaForm syntax
state contactEmail = ""
state wantsUpdates = true

form id="contact"
  input name="contactEmail"
    type="email"
    label="Email address"
    required=true

  checkbox name="wantsUpdates"
    label="Send me updates"

  submit "Send message"

  success
    text "Message received."
Working browser example

Contact form

Try submitting with an invalid email, then correct it.

Uses native browser email validation.
Form submitted successfully. This is a local demo only.

Input type catalogue

Text, email, password, number, telephone, URL, textarea, checkbox and select.

Currently unchecked.
This contact form does not send data to a server. Forma's client-side submit event can expose submitted values to client-side code, but real data collection needs a trusted backend, validation and appropriate security controls.
10 · Compatibility

Keep the old. Build the new.

A place to document legacy syntax that remains supported as Forma evolves.

Older styleIllustrative
# Earlier project syntax
site "My website"
  page "/"
    text "Hello world"
Current styleIllustrative
site "My website"
  theme
    color.accent = "#c5f467"

  page "/"
    container
      title "Hello world"
      text "Built with Forma."

These examples illustrate the idea of compatibility. They do not establish that every older syntax variant is accepted by the current parser. Refer to LANGUAGE.md for the authoritative syntax reference.

The bigger picture

A language should make the good parts easier.

Forma brings structure, styling and interaction into one expressive workflow. The goal is not to replace everything in web development. It is to make building thoughtful interfaces simpler.
